text:
Absolutely — here are a few vegetarian, spicy dinners that fit the one-handed / one-pan brief and won’t ask much of you on a baby-sleep schedule:

1. Chickpea coconut curry with spinach
   - Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and curry paste.
   - Add chickpeas + coconut milk, simmer 10 minutes, then stir in spinach.
   - Serve over rice or with naan.
   - Why it works: one pot, very forgiving, and leftovers reheat well.

2. Sheet-pan harissa vegetables with halloumi or tofu
   - Roast peppers, zucchini, red onion, and chickpeas with olive oil + harissa.
   - Add halloumi for the last few minutes, or roast tofu on the tray.
   - Finish with lemon and yogurt.
   - Why it works: almost no active cooking, just a tray and an oven.

3. Spicy peanut noodles with tofu
   - Toss noodles with peanut butter, soy sauce, chili crisp, lime, and a little hot water.
   - Add quick-sautéed greens and tofu.
   - Why it works: fast, one-pan-ish, and easy to eat one-handed.

4. Lentil taco skillet
   - Simmer lentils with salsa, cumin, smoked paprika, and corn.
   - Top with cheese, avocado, and hot sauce; scoop into tortillas.
   - Why it works: hearty, spicy, and all in one skillet.

5. Kimchi fried rice with egg or tofu
   - Fry garlic, kimchi, and cooked rice; add egg or tofu and sesame oil.
   - Why it works: very fast, very spicy, and ideal for leftover rice.

If you want, I can turn this into a 5-night plan or a shopping list.
